title: First 30 days - hidden dependencies & knowledge transfer playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a practical, lightweight playbook to surface, track, and remediate "hidden" dependencies new hires hit in their first 30 days. Hidden deps = anything not in the official checklist but critical for job success: undocumented scripts, shadow owners (subject matter experts), service knobs in infra, local config forks, or cross-team weekly rituals.

Audience:
- Hiring manager
- Buddy / mentor
- New hire (IC or PM)
- People Ops & onboarding coordinator

Core principles (short):
- Treat unknowns as first-class tickets (triage, owner, ETA).
- Make visible the network of people and artifacts, not just systems.
- Create reusable micro-docs (1–2 paragraphs + command snippets).
- Prioritize access and fail-open paths early (48–72h goal for critical systems).

How to use: quick run-through timeline
- Day 0 (pre-start): send "shadow-owner" ask to hiring manager; pre-provision common read-only accesses; add new hire to onboarding Slack channel.
- Day 1–3: run a rapid discovery sprint with buddy to list 10 unknowns; create tickets for each unknown in "ONBOARD-DEPS" queue.
- Day 4–14: weekly small TTR (time-to-resolve) sprints: 3 highest-impact deps remediated per week.
- Day 15–30: handoff micro-docs into team docs, tag owners, and close tickets.

Discovery checklist (use in a 45–60m working session):
- People map: who to ping when X fails? (name, team channel, backup)
- Infra artifacts: config repos, feature flags, deployment shortcuts, secret paths
- Data dependencies: where is canonical data? which DBs have read-only policies?
- CI/CD oddities: manual gating steps, flaky jobs, special env vars
- Local dev quirks: ports, scripts that must be run, container overrides
- Observability blindspots: dashboards that exist but aren’t owned, alert floods to expect
- On-call overlaps: which pods/teams escalate to whom?
- Regulatory/Compliance steps: extra approvals or audits for customer data access

Ticket template for "ONBOARD-DEPS" queue (copy into tracker):
- Title (short): e.g., "Hidden DB creds for analytics worker"
- Reporter: new hire name + date
- Impact: low/med/high (impact on new hire or on release velocity)
- Short description: 1–2 sentences describing the unknown
- Repro/triage steps: minimal commands or steps to reproduce the gap
- Proposed mitigation: quick workaround + long-term fix idea
- Owner: person (or team) assigned
- ETA: target resolution date
- Docs: link to any micro-doc created
- Status: triage / in_progress / resolved / deferred

Buddy playbook (for the mentor/buddy):
- First 72h: two 30m paired sessions to run discovery checklist and to get core paths working locally.
- Week 1: introduce 5 cross-team contacts (not just names: explain context of relationship).
- Week 2: shadow the new hire in their first incident or deploy (if applicable).
- Ongoing: keep the open deps list visible in weekly 1:1s until cleared.

Micro-doc guidance (what a good micro-doc looks like):
- Title (one line)
- Problem statement (1 sentence)
- Quick steps / commands (3–6 lines, copy-paste friendly)
- Who to contact if this fails (name + slack channel)
- One-sentence long-term suggestion
- Tags / keywords
Example:
  Title: "Run model-serving locally against staging embedding store"
  Problem: dev can't start server because embedding store migrations are behind.
  Quick steps:
    - git clone infra/embeddings && ./scripts/bootstrap-staging.sh
    - export EMB_STORE_URL=staging-emb.local:5432
    - ./dev/run-server --no-cache
  Contact: Marco Alvarez (infra-embeddings), #infra-embeddings
  Suggestion: add an automated health-check that warns if migrations are out-of-sync

Prioritization rubric for deps
- Urgent (blocker): prevents core onboarding tasks, must resolve in 72h.
- High: major friction, reduces ramp speed by >50%, resolve within 2 weeks.
- Medium: nice-to-have for productivity, resolve within 30d.
- Low: long-term cleanup; capture for later backlog grooming.

Sample 30-day plan (concise, to hand to hiring manager):
- Day 0–1: access & comms verified; run discovery checklist with buddy; create ONBOARD-DEPS tickets.
- Day 2–7: fix 2 urgent deps (owner assigned), create micro-docs for each; manager check-in on blocked items.
- Day 8–14: close or document all high-priority deps; schedule cross-team introductions for medium items.
- Day 15–21: run a retro with new hire & buddy: "what surprised you?" capture learnings.
- Day 22–30: tidy micro-docs into team handbook, tag owner, mark tickets resolved or backlog.

Retro prompts (use in week 3 session):
- What took longer than expected and why?
- Who saved you early on? Who was missing?
- Which artifacts were missing or misleading?
- If we had to onboard 5 people next month, what would we change?

Risk register (quick starter table as bullets):
- Secrets not in vault -> mitigation: emergency temp creds + rotate + ticket to vault team (48h)
- Single-person SME for critical infra -> mitigation: schedule shadowing and add runbook in 7d
- Required approvals taking >2 weeks -> mitigation: escalate to hiring manager and create expedited compliance checklist

Operational notes (practical tips):
- Reserve a 60m "dependency discovery" slot on day 2 in the calendar for manager + buddy + new hire.
- Use short-lived, audited credentials for early access; avoid blanket org-level permissions.
- Encourage creation of micro-docs in the same PR where the fix is made.
- Keep ONBOARD-DEPS queue tag visible in team board and add a weekly swimlane for 30-day hires.

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Should we create a central catalog of micro-docs filtered by role? (people-ops owns decision)
- Default owner for infra-level unknowns: infra-sre or the most recent committer? (edge cases exist)
- How to handle contractors with limited access needs vs full-time hires? (policy needed)

Templates to copy (paste into new ticket / micro-doc)
- New ticket headline: "ONBOARD-DEPS: [role] - short problem headline"
- Micro-doc header: title | tl;dr | commands | contacts | proposed fix

Example filled ticket (short):
- Title: ONBOARD-DEPS: backend-eng - Missing analytics DB read view
- Reporter: Nora Kim (new hire) 2025-07-09
- Impact: High
- Short desc: Analytics queries failing for local dev; historical view missing in test schema.
- Repro: run scripts/data_load.sh -> failed on create_view analytics_view
- Workaround: use staging_view and set EXPORT_OVERRIDE=true
- Owner: Marco Alvarez
- ETA: 2025-07-14
- Docs: link to micro-doc in team wiki

Measuring success (signals after 30d):
- New hires report ramp friction score <= 3 (1-5 scale; lower is better) on hidden-deps survey
- ONBOARD-DEPS queue average time-to-resolve for urgent tickets <= 4 days
- 75% of micro-docs created during onboarding are reused by at least one other hire in 90d

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Pilot with two upcoming backend hires in July; collect 3 retro stories each.
- Share quick checklist with hiring managers in next week’s people-ops sync.

Quick links (placeholders):
- Team handbook: confluence://team/handbook
- ONBOARD-DEPS board: https://linear.app/redwood/board/ONBOARD-DEPS
- Micro-doc examples folder: drive://company/misc/onboard-microdocs

End.
